annotations.shape: one text/plain us-ascii message in which ONE header line is terminated by a lone CR (`X-Lone: one\rX-Next: two\r\n`), so two fields share what a CRLF-only reader would call one line
annotations.raw_fixture: hand-written bytes in tools/write_raw_fixtures.py, frozen in fixtures/raw/SHA256SUMS -- a lone CR is exactly the byte a generator's CRLF writer cannot emit
annotations.phase_0_facts: container.*, headers.fields (nine fields: the lone CR is a line terminator, so X-Lone and X-Next are two fields), part.tree, part.regions, part.gaps, body.preamble_epilogue, decode.chain and body.content_sha256. Decision 17 keeps the walker's line model, so a lone CR is a line terminator today and the phase-0 facts record that
annotations.phase_1_facts: document.axes, and the gap body.lone_cr_line_terminator in gaps.later (a Phase 1 id the walker does not emit today)
annotations.labels_are_typed: every value was read out of the fixture bytes with a hex-editor-style line dump and typed by a model from the RFC and design rules (D2, decision 17), never copied out of the walker; labels_provenance is spec because a model wrote them, not a person
annotations.span_conventions: a lone CR is a line terminator, so X-Lone's raw_span ends at the CR (12 bytes) and X-Next's spans the following line; the regions still tile the message exactly
annotations.expected_gaps: body.lone_cr_line_terminator (Phase 1, in gaps.later) on part 1; no phase-0 gap
annotations.not_yet_labelled: addresses, the Date projection, encoded words, body views, attachments, statuses, thread edges and TimeEvents

value: a lone CR terminates a header line; decision 17 keeps the walker's line model, so the CR is a terminator and the standing gap is recorded rather than the framing being changed
